name: css_animation_out
description: -azul-animation-out DRIVES THE ZOMBIE. #sidebar declares `-azul-animation-out: flyOutRight 1s` (builtin table; no @keyframes needed). Unmounting it retains the subtree as a zombie whose motion comes from the compiled track (translate right + width narrowing + clip to the frozen rect), NOT the default slide. The zombie must survive mid-flight ticks and reap exactly when the track completes - a zombie that outlives its animation is a leak, one that dies early truncates the exit. Companion pins: window::tests::builtin_fly_out_right_shifts_right_and_narrows_to_zero (track shape) and stylesheet_keyframes_shadow_the_builtin_table (author @keyframes take precedence over the builtin of the same name). DISCRIMINATOR: a track-driven exit runs on the compiled track alone - the manager holds NO spring for it - so right after the remount the manager holds exactly ONE animation (the CARD's move as it takes over the vacated space) - active:1,zombies:1. The default-slide fallback adds a SECOND spring for the sidebar exit (active:2), which is exactly what the NC sabotage (seeding disabled) produced when this assert was first tightened.
